summary: Tested the owner password change, cohort result analysis (rank, charts, 25 insights, per-question peer stats), gpt-6-astra AI solutions (API and UI), the PDF report with AI text, mobile overflow at 390px, and a chapter-test regression. Everything passes except one critical failure: the PDF report for any Mock 01 attempt fails. Its job ends in 'failed' because matplotlib mathtext cannot parse the LaTeX that gpt-6-astra writes. Backend pytest: 8/9 passed. Frontend: all checked flows pass.

critical.issue: The PDF job fails for every attempt on a mock that has ready AI solutions (all of Mock 01). In reports.py render_report, report.rich() on the AI parts calls math_png(). That raises ValueError ('This typed equation cannot be exported faithfully') on LaTeX that matplotlib mathtext does not support: \frac12 without braces, \boxed, \text, \left/\right, \quad\Rightarrow and so on. I scanned the 184 ready solutions and 127 of them (69%) contain at least one formula that cannot be rendered. The job retries and ends 'failed'. Before this change the PDF worked (iteration_93, Mock 50, no AI).

minor.issue: sections[] comes back in Mongo $group order (Mathematics, Chemistry, ...), not paper order. The frontend matches by name, so nothing breaks, but any consumer that relies on order would get it wrong.

issues: The copy still says 'No worked solutions are included.' and 'Every mock passed ...'. This now contradicts the AI solutions progress chip next to it.
The 142-cell heatmap is about 21 rows tall at 7 cells per row, so it takes up a lot of scrolling. Consider smaller cells or grouping by section. Minor.

The insight count is not always 25. A chapter test showed '21-point deep insight' because cards with null values are dropped. Mock 01 shows exactly 25. If the user wants 25 every time, add fallback insights.

action_items: CRITICAL: Make the PDF tolerate AI LaTeX. In reports.py, render the AI solution parts with a safe path: catch math_png ValueError per formula and fall back to plain text, or normalise the LaTeX first (\frac12 -> \frac{1}{2}, strip \boxed{}/\text{}/\left/\right, replace \quad). Keep the strict validation only for owner-typed question math. The Report.rich() call at reports.py line ~200 is the failing call.
Optionally tell gpt-6-astra in the prompt to use only matplotlib-compatible LaTeX (braced \frac, no \boxed/\text).
Update the stale 'No worked solutions are included' copy in MockBookPanel.
Optionally guarantee 25 insights with fallback cards, or keep the dynamic count.
critical_code_review_comments: reports.py: one bad AI formula aborts the whole PDF. AI text is untrusted, so render it best-effort.
mock_solutions.lane(): `except (AstraUnavailable, Exception)` is redundant. It also hides programming errors behind a warning that logs only the class name.
mock_solutions.solution_id depends on q.get('answer'). If an attempt's question snapshot ever lacks 'answer', for_questions will silently return not_queued. It works today (142/142 matched).
cohorts.MIN_SAMPLE=1 means a lone student sees 'rank #1 of 1, percentile 100'. This is intended per the spec, and the early-sample note is shown.

rca of the issue: PDF failure. Repro: complete any Mock 01 attempt and POST /api/attempts/{id}/report. The job ends 'failed'. Backend log: ParseSyntaxException 'Expected \frac{num}{den}, found 12' on '$$K=\frac12 mv^2\quad\Rightarrow ...$$', raised from reports.py math_png -> Report.rich (line 118) -> render_report (line 200). Cause: AI solution text uses KaTeX-style LaTeX, and matplotlib mathtext supports only a subset. The strict validator that blocks owner input is applied to untrusted AI text, so the exception propagates and kills the job. Fix: render AI formulas best-effort and fall back to text.
